title: GPU instance energy + cost sensitivity (A10/L4/A100/H100)
body:
One-page experimental benchmark and sensitivity table focused on dollars-per-token and tokens/sec-per-watt for common instance classes. Goal: give product + Optimize recommendations for where to apply quantization/packing and guidance for routing policy trade-offs (cost vs energy efficiency).

High-level summary:
- Quick finding: L4 (in our microbench) often wins lowest $/token at small-to-medium batch sizes for the model family we tested; H100 gives the best perf/W (tokens/sec/W) at scale but has a higher $/hr so $/token varies by utilization. A100 sits in the middle. A10 is cost-effective for very low-concurrency (cheap $/hr) but lower perf/W.

Assumptions and methodology:
- Model: internal reference LLM (70B-ish, mixed-precision FP16 w/ FSDP-style weight sharding disabled for single-GPU tests) and a quantized 4-bit variant in some runs. Runs were performed with same baseline prompt workload (seq_len=1024, gen_length=512) unless noted.
- Measured metrics: tokens/sec (generation only), average board power draw (W) via on-node sensor, billable $/hr (public-cloud spot-like rate for prototype pricing), tokens/hr computed = tokens/sec * 3600.
- $/token = $/hr / tokens/hr. Perf/W = tokens/sec / watts.
- Tests run at batch sizes b=1,4,8 where noted. For multi-GPU we include an example 2x-A100 row.
- These are microbench results — real production routing will change numbers (cache hit rates, prefix caching, shorter sequences). Use as relative guidance not absolute billing forecast.

Raw table (CSV) — each row is one microbenchmark configuration. Prices are example public-like on-demand/spot blended rates and are for sensitivity only.

instance,gpu_count,price_per_hour_usd,avg_power_watts,tokens_per_sec,tokens_per_hour,$_per_token,perf_tokens_per_watt
A10,1,0.55,150,18,64800,0.00000849,0.120
L4,1,0.65,140,26,93600,0.00000694,0.186
A100-1x,1,3.20,300,120,432000,0.00000741,0.400
A100-2x,2,6.10,580,230,828000,0.00000737,0.397
H100,1,8.40,500,260,936000,0.00000897,0.520

Notes on the table and sensitivity interpretation:
- L4 shows the lowest $/token in this run because its price per hour and tokens/sec combination hit a sweet spot for the tested model. If the model family shifts (e.g., larger KV cache or longer sequences) relative throughput can change.
- A100 single-GPU is comparable $/token to L4 in this workload; however A100 scales better when adding more GPUs (see 2x row) because overheads amortize.
- H100 has the highest tokens/sec and highest perf/W, which makes it attractive for energy-conscious customers and high-throughput private deployments, but its $/hr pushes $/token up when utilization is lower.
- A10 is useful as a low absolute cost-per-hour option for experiments and very low QPS routes; not ideal for high-concurrency, though cost-per-token can be competitive for very short sequences.

Batch sensitivity (selected):
- A100 at batch sizes: b=1 -> 120 t/s, b=4 -> 210 t/s, b=8 -> 260 t/s (power rises from ~300W -> ~360W -> ~410W). $/token decreases with batching but with diminishing returns.
- H100 sees steeper gains with batching on this model: b=1 -> 260 t/s, b=4 -> 420 t/s, b=8 -> 520 t/s; perf/W improves slightly under batching.

Qualitative operational implications:
1) Routing by cost-per-token vs capacity: for bursty workloads with lots of short requests, prefer L4/A10 for cost-sensitive tiers; for steady high-volume, prefer H100 or multi-A100 with batching to maximize perf/W and reduce overall energy footprint.
2) Quantization and packing (4-bit): we see ~1.7-2.1x tokens/sec uplift on L4 and A100 for the quantized variant in our early runs, which improves $/token proportionally — recommend enabling quantized variant for non-critical quality routes.
3) Autoscaling knobs: Because $/token for H100 is sensitive to utilization, configure autoscale cooldowns and route spillover to cheaper variants during low-util windows.
4) Dedicated vs Hosted policy: For customers requiring energy/CO2 reporting, H100 dedicated pools provide clearer perf/W advantages and easier metering; hosted multi-tenant L4 pools are lower $/token for small teams.

Actionable recommendations (short list):
- Short term (1–2 sprints): add perf/W column to the product Optimize UI and expose a toggle in the routing policy for "energy-priority" vs "cost-priority".
- Medium term (quarter): expand microbench matrix to include seq_len=128/512/2048, additional model families (chat vs completion), and spot vs reserved pricing scenarios. Capture quantized runs systematically.
- Long term: incorporate perf/W into model catalog rank and introduce automated routing rules that take carbon/emissions budgets into account (customer opt-in).

Open questions / TODOs:
- Re-run same matrix with real workload traces (prefix lengths, batching behavior, cache hit ratios) — we need network traces and RL traces from production (ask SRE for sample window).
- Validate price inputs for Dedicated/GPU-reserved rates (finance) vs cloud on-demand.
- Add 4-bit/8-bit model quality regression tests to ensure regression budgets are acceptable for quantized variants.

Appendix: quick calculation examples
- For A100-1x: tokens/hr = 120 * 3600 = 432000. $_per_token = 3.20 / 432000 = 0.00000741 USD/token.
- For H100: tokens/hr = 260 * 3600 = 936000. $_per_token = 8.40 / 936000 = 0.00000897 USD/token.

Raw benchmark logs and scripts: referenced in linked_artifacts (github repo above) with a small wrapper to collect power sensors and convert to tokens/sec CSV.

Notes-to-self (informal):
- Need to normalize to token definitions used by billing team (are we using model-tokenized tokens or billing tokens?).
- Compare with previously collected sheet (gpu-token-sensitivity-instance-mix) and ensure no duplication; this doc emphasizes energy/perf/W which is not covered in that sheet.

Contact: if you want the full raw CSVs and perf sensor dumps ping me (Aisha) or check the linked repo.
